title: Localization of a ring induces a flat monomorphism of spectra
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset containing $1$, and let $B=S^{-1}A$ be the ring of fractions [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. The morphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by $a\mapsto a/1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and is a monomorphism: for every scheme $T$ and morphisms $u,v:T\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, the equality $h\circ u=h\circ v$ implies $u=v$. No Noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is imposed; $0\in S$ is allowed.
